title: Changing Model and Keeping Equipment Rental and Demo Kit Longer
content:
**How many times may a rider change model while the kit is out?**

A rider may change to a different model or size while the kit is out, up to the number of changes the package allows. Changes are counted on the agreement, so a rider who has used the package's allowance is offered a new agreement at the day rate rather than a further change.

**What does a change cost?**

The clause reading "Packages that include changes carry no fee for them; the rest carry the package's change fee for every change after the first refit for a genuine misfit, which is never charged" is **no longer in force**. It has been superseded by the current basis on which a change of model is priced, and is repeated here only so that the withdrawn wording is not applied. Every package of the Equipment Rental and Demo line keeps the change figures held against it: whether changes sit inside the package, the change fee, and the number of changes one agreement may carry.

**On what terms may an agreement be extended?**

The clause reading "An agreement may be extended while the kit is still out, where the package allows it and by no more than the package's extension limit; the extra days are charged at the rate the agreement was written on and the package's extension fee is raised on top" is likewise **no longer in force**, superseded by the current basis on which an extension is priced. The package's extension figures — whether extension is allowed, the extension fee and the extension limit in days — stand unchanged.

**When is an extension recorded?**

An extension is recorded before the kit falls due, not after: kit already overdue is handled as a late hand-in and the extension route is closed.

**Is a season lease extended?**

A season lease is not extended at all; it runs to the end of the season it was written for.

### Points of judgement

**A rider on a package that allows one change who has already had one.** The allowance counted on that agreement is used. What is offered is a new agreement at the day rate, not a second change on the standing one.

**Kit that fell due yesterday.** The kit is already overdue, so it is handled as a late hand-in.

**Kit due tomorrow.** The kit has not yet fallen due, so an extension may still be recorded on the agreement.

An agreement may be extended while the kit is still out, where the package allows it and by no more than the package's extension limit; the extra days are charged at the rate the agreement was written on and the package's extension fee is raised on top.
